findings.description: `parseCall` never checks that the usage fields are numbers. If a worker writes `input_tokens` as a string, `contextOf` joins the strings instead of adding. `percentile` returns that string, and `tokens()` prints it raw through `formatRow` with no `sanitizeReason`, so ESC/CSI sequences from a worker's transcript reach the operator's terminal. A non-string `effort` or `model` crashes the command, and negative counts skew the totals.
findings.body:
**Usage counts from a worker's transcript reach the operator's terminal unsanitized**

A session writes its own transcript directory (ADR 0067: "the newest `.jsonl` there is whatever it put there"). ADR 0122 *Print* scrubs model, effort and tool names because they come "from a file a worker can write". The usage numbers come from the same file, and nothing checks them:

```ts
if (!usage || !model || model.startsWith('<')) return undefined;
const {
  input_tokens: input = 0,
  ...
} = usage;
```

The `= 0` defaults only replace `undefined`. Here is what each kind of bad value does:

- **String `input_tokens`** (or `cache_read_input_tokens`): `contextOf` concatenates instead of adding. `percentile`'s `a - b` comparator gives NaN, so the string stays in the list and is returned as the median, p90 and first-request floor. `tokens()` falls through to `String(n)`, and `formatRow` prints it with no `sanitizeReason`. A planted line such as `{"type":"assistant","timestamp":"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z","requestId":"r","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","usage":{"input_tokens":"\u001b[2J..."}}}` clears the operator's screen and draws the worker's own text in its place. The total cost and the row's cost come out as `$NaN`.
- **Negative counts:** these are accepted and take spend off the total.
- **Non-string `effort`:** crashes `sanitizeReason(row.effort)` in the text report.
- **Non-string `model`:** crashes at `model.startsWith`, on both the text and `--json` paths.

`--json` itself is not open to the escape injection, because `JSON.stringify` and the DEL/C1 rewrite cover it.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/8c949e7c178d9f77fd8c7e5fc624ac1593ad9add/src/core/usage-report.service.ts#L184-L198
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/8c949e7c178d9f77fd8c7e5fc624ac1593ad9add/src/core/usage-report.service.ts#L483-L495

**Fix:** check types where the data comes in.

- Treat any count that is not `typeof n === 'number' && Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0` as 0.
- Require `typeof model === 'string'`.
- Take `effort` only when it is a string, and use `'unknown'` otherwise.
- Optionally, clamp `write1h` to `written` so that `write5m` cannot go negative.

findings.description: `blocksOf` treats any array as `ContentBlock[]`, so a worker-written `"content":[null]` throws at `block.content` / `block.type`. Only the `readFileSync` call is inside a `try`, so one planted line crashes `pup usage` on every run, and the error does not name the file. A non-string `tool_use.name` likewise crashes `sanitizeReason(t.tool)` in `formatCarry`.
findings.body:
**One malformed line in a worker's transcript stops `pup usage` from running**

```ts
function blocksOf(content: unknown): ContentBlock[] {
  return Array.isArray(content) ? (content as ContentBlock[]) : [];
}
```

The cast does not check the array's elements. The crash path:

- `parseLine`'s `try` covers only `JSON.parse`, and `scanLine` has no `try`.
- `noteOrigin` reads the first `user` entry before the window check.
- So a line `{"type":"user","message":{"content":[null]}}` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'content')` in `textOf`, whatever `--since` is.
- The `usage` action has no catch, and `fatalExitCode` rethrows a TypeError, so the command dies without naming the file.

The same applies at `block.type` in `noteAssistant` and `noteToolResults`.

Separately, line 236 checks only that `block.name` is truthy. A `tool_use` named `5` or `{}` is stored, and later crashes `sanitizeReason(t.tool)` in `formatCarry`, because `sanitizeReason` calls `.replace`.

ADR 0067 states the rule this breaks: "An unreadable transcript is a reading that degrades, not a surface that dies". This PR's own test checks that a non-JSON line and a `broken.jsonl` directory degrade the same way.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/8c949e7c178d9f77fd8c7e5fc624ac1593ad9add/src/core/usage-report.service.ts#L169-L171
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/8c949e7c178d9f77fd8c7e5fc624ac1593ad9add/src/core/usage-report.service.ts#L234-L242

**Fix:** both edits are needed, because neither covers the other.

1. Keep only object blocks:

```ts
function blocksOf(content: unknown): ContentBlock[] {
  if (!Array.isArray(content)) return [];
  return content.filter((block): block is ContentBlock => typeof block === 'object' && block !== null);
}
```

2. Require a string tool name at line 236: `block.type === 'tool_use' && block.id && typeof block.name === 'string'`.

findings.description: Nothing stops `workerDirsOf` from returning the checkout's own transcript dir, and sources are never deduped by file path. A sessions row whose `worktree_path` is the repo path (decision 67 treats that column as session-writable) makes every console, conductor and utility transcript count twice: once as `worker` and once as its real class. That doubles the total cost. Exclude `transcriptDir(repoPath, claudeDir)` from the worker set, or dedupe sources by file.

Tool names are recorded only in `noteAssistant`, which runs only for entries inside the window. So when a `tool_use` falls before `--since` and its `tool_result` falls after, the result is counted and carried under `unknown` instead of its tool. Recording `tool_use` ids from every assistant entry, whatever its timestamp, fixes it.

The per-row 'cost split' prints only the read, write and output shares. `costOf` also computes the uncached-input part (`parts.input`), but it is never reported, so the shares don't add up to 100%. For lightly cached rows such as headless utility calls, a line like 'read 0.0%, write 0.0%, output 33.3%' leaves most of the cost unexplained. Add an input share, or label the line so it is clear input is left out.

`readTranscript` calls `readFileSync(file, 'utf8')` on any `*.jsonl` name with no regular-file check and no `O_NONBLOCK`. A worker can plant a FIFO (`mkfifo x.jsonl`) or a symlink to `/dev/zero` in its own transcript dir, which hangs `pup usage` or grows its memory without bound. Open with `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK`, `fstat`, and skip non-regular files, as `readPlainFile` in `src/adapters/capability.utils.ts` already does (decision 96). `latestContextTokens` has the same gap today.

`sourcesIn` walks each dir with `readdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })` but keeps only depth 0 and `<x>/subagents/*.jsonl`. A symlinked top-level dir matching the `.worktrees` prefix can point the walk at the operator's whole `$HOME`. One unreadable subdirectory (e.g. `mkdir -m 000`) throws, and that blanks every transcript in the dir without any error. A two-level listing, with its own `try` per subagents dir, avoids both and drops the regexes.

`const CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4` redeclares a constant already exported from `src/core/profile.constants.ts:5` and used by the profile compiler. If that estimate is ever refined, tool-carry tokens will quietly stop matching profile-budget tokens. Import it from `./profile.constants.js` instead.

Conductor detection matches the literal `'# Pupitre conductor '`, which only happens to equal the heading `buildConductorContext` writes (`profile-compiler.service.ts:1275`). Rewording that heading would silently move every conductor transcript into `console`, and the test builds its own copy of the literal, so it would not catch the change. Export one heading-prefix constant and use it in all three places.

The text format lives in core (`formatUsageReport`), but the JSON format and its DEL/C1 `\uXXXX` escaping are built inline in the CLI action, against AGENTS.md's 'src/cli/ stays thin; logic lives in src/core/'. As a result, the escaping can only be tested end to end. A `formatUsageReportJson` next to `formatUsageReport` would let the action just choose a formatter and make the escape test a unit test.

The tests 'reads the transcripts of the config dir --session-env names' and 'escapes DEL and C1 in a planted name under --json' repeat the same ~17-line setup: config dir, `saveSessionEnv`, env stubs, `transcriptDir`, and the transcript write. A local helper inside `describe('usage')` that takes extra entry fields would leave each test showing only what it checks.
